zh: 一串字母能重排成回文，当且仅当出现奇数次的字母至多一种；所以只需关心每种字母出现次数的奇偶，用 26 位掩码表示。
取任意根，记 mask[u] 为根到 u 路径的奇偶掩码；u 到 v 路径的掩码等于 mask[u] XOR mask[v]（公共部分出现两次被抵消）。点对合法当且仅当两个掩码相等或只差一位。
BFS/迭代遍历求出所有 mask；按遍历顺序处理节点，用哈希表记录此前每种掩码出现的次数，对当前掩码查询它本身以及翻转 26 位中任意一位的 27 个掩码并累加，然后再把当前掩码计入；答案用 64 位整数。
en: A multiset of letters can be rearranged into a palindrome exactly when at most one letter occurs an odd number of times, so only the parity of each letter's count matters, which fits in a 26-bit mask.

Pick any root and let mask[u] be the parity mask of the root-to-u path; the mask of the u–v path is mask[u] XOR mask[v] (the shared part appears twice and cancels). A pair is nice exactly when the two masks are equal or differ in one bit.

Compute every mask with BFS or another iterative traversal; process nodes in that order with a hash map counting how often each mask has appeared so far: for the current mask, add the counts of the mask itself and of the 26 masks with one bit flipped (27 lookups), then record the current mask; keep the answer in a 64-bit integer.

explanationEn:
## Original OCR, examples and full ranges

Files OA LIST/WeRide_OA/018–024 in fixed commit e66f809f4c953bce129f68491726176615db6afc give the complete numNicePairs problem: an undirected tree with edge weights 1..26 corresponding to a..z; if the edge letters on the unique shortest path between two distinct nodes can be rearranged arbitrarily into a palindrome, the pair is a nice pair. Count unordered pairs of distinct nodes. The five-node all-A tree in 023/024 gives 10 and lists all distinct pairs, explicitly excluding self-pairs and counting each pair in only one direction.

The original constraints in 020/021 are complete: 1≤n≤100000, m=n−1, endpoints in 1..n, edge weights 1..26, and the tree's diameter is strictly less than 1000 (in edges). The diameter limit is not dropped, so a 100000-node long chain is invalid and cannot serve as an official full-range test. The input keeps the standard protocol of 021 directly: n m, then m lines of u v w, with nodes uniformly 1-based. n=1 is valid and the answer is 0. The return type is long; the maximum is 100000×99999/2=4999950000, which needs 64 bits.

The three public examples keep, in full, 9 from 019, 7 from 021/022 and 10 from 023/024. Note that the illustrated tree in 018 has edges 1–2, 2–3, 2–4, 3–5, while the one in 019 has 1–2, 2–3, 3–4, 3–5; although both have weights 2,1,1,1, the topologies differ, so the 9 from 019 must not be applied to 018. The site uses 018 as a separate hidden test whose answer, 8, was computed independently pair by pair; the public editorial explicitly distinguishes the two graphs rather than mixing sources. In example 019, BAA must be rearranged into ABA, which directly shows the condition is not whether the original path string is already a palindrome.

## Approach

Choose any root and compute, for each node, the parity mask of the counts of the 26 letters on the root-to-node path. The mask of the path from u to v in the tree equals the XOR of the two root-path masks, because the shared part appears twice and cancels. A string can be rearranged into a palindrome if and only if at most one character has an odd count, so a pair is valid when the two masks are equal or differ in exactly one bit.

Traverse the nodes and keep a hash table with the frequency of each mask seen so far. Query the current mask and the masks obtained by flipping each of the 26 bits, accumulate their frequencies, and then add the current node to the table. Use an iterative traversal to avoid depending on the recursion stack.

## Proof of correctness

Apart from a possible middle character, the positions of a palindrome pair up, so at most one character with an odd count is necessary. Conversely, put half of each character on the left, mirror it on the right, and put the only possible odd character in the middle to build a palindrome, so the condition is also sufficient.

The parts of the two root paths from the root down to the common ancestor are XORed twice and vanish, and the remaining edges are exactly the unique path from u to v. So the path parity condition is equivalent to mask[u] XOR mask[v] having at most one set bit, i.e. the masks being equal or differing in one bit.

Before the current node is processed, the hash table contains only earlier nodes, and the 27 query masks are all distinct, so they enumerate exactly the earlier nodes that form a valid pair with the current one. The node is inserted only after querying, so it is never paired with itself. Each unordered pair of distinct nodes is checked exactly once, when its later endpoint is processed, so there are no omissions and no duplicates, and the final sum is correct.

## Complexity

Traversal and building the graph take O(n); each node does 27 hash lookups, for expected time O(26n) and space O(n). The hash uses SplitMix64 with a runtime seed, so that crafted masks colliding in one bucket cannot easily attack a fixed integer hash. Hash complexity is still an expected bound, not a deterministic worst case. Full-size random trees and relabeled trees exercise many distinct masks, and verification records the actual number of distinct masks. Masks need only 26 bits; counts and the answer use 64 bits. The native reference package uses 3 seconds/256 MiB, and the full original range and diameter constraint are not reduced.

## Independent verification

A small oracle traverses the tree from each start node, explicitly copying the 26-dimensional path frequency, and counts the odd frequencies directly when it reaches a larger-numbered endpoint, without using root masks or hash pairing at all. 163 unique small inputs were actually run against the native reference. In addition, all trees with n≤5 built from increasing parent indices with two-letter edge weights were enumerated and verified with independent path counting.

The large-range oracle starts from a different root, computes all masks first and groups them offline by frequency: identical masks contribute f(f−1)/2, and two groups differing in one bit contribute f·g counted only from the smaller mask's side, without the reference's online query-then-insert process. All-one-letter trees are additionally checked with the closed form n(n−1)/2, and star trees with n−1+ΣC(number of leaves with the same letter, 2). Every input is checked at generation time for connectivity, acyclicity, the edge count, and the true diameter found by two BFS passes. Full-size cases cover stars, balanced trees, all 26 letters, random relabeling, and broom trees of diameter 999, without using the invalid full-length chain. Negative controls include counting ordered pairs twice, self-pairs, and a wrong single-letter-path restriction; all official negative controls must exit normally.
